severityMeaning.Error: element or its steel not trusted; blocks finalization
severityMeaning.Warning: quantities produced, human review; some block finalization

codes.description: schemaVersion is not one this engine understands.
No provenance block, or provenance.type is not a known category.
Provenance mixes synthetic and ETABS-verified categories (e.g. synthetic with etabs_verified=true, or a capture without an ETABS version).
model.units.length is not one of m, mm, cm, ft, in.
Two or more elements share an ID but differ in content. All copies are rejected because the true object cannot be determined.
Zero-length frame, polygon with < 3 points, non-planar, zero-area or self-intersecting polygon.
A coordinate is non-finite or larger than the configured maximum magnitude.
A section dimension (width, depth, diameter, thickness) is zero or negative.
The element references a section that is not defined in the snapshot.
The section shape is not supported for quantity take-off, or does not suit the element type.
The element or its reinforcement references a material not defined in the snapshot.
The material exists but its type is not Concrete, Steel or Rebar, so the element cannot be classified.
The element has no story. It is reported under '<unassigned>'.
The element's story is not in model.stories. It is reported under '<unassigned>'.
A rebar material density is zero or negative. Steel using it is unknown.
A rebar material density is outside the configured plausible band. Steel using it is unknown.
Reinforcement data is invalid (spacing <= 0, diameter <= 0, count <= 0, missing length for area elements, ...). Steel is unknown.
The reinforcement source category does not match the component types supplied, or is not a known category.
A RequiredArea component references a design result that is absent or does not cover the member.
The referenced result is not designed or has an unsupported status. Demand steel remains unknown.
The design result belongs to a different member. Demand steel remains unknown.
Design results have invalid/nonfinite/negative demands, duplicate stations, ambiguous result records or conversion overflow.
A mesh layout was given for a host that is not a rectangle and no explicit region was supplied.
A dimension is implausibly large and would be typical if divided by 1000 - probably a unit error. The value is NOT auto-corrected.
Element steel mass per m3 of concrete exceeds the density of steel - physically impossible. The steel value is discarded (unknown).
An analytical/mesh child references a parent that does not exist.
The design result used for required reinforcement is flagged stale (model changed after design).
Steel quantification was requested but the element has no reinforcement data. Steel is unknown, not zero.
Two slabs on the same story and plane overlap in plan. Both are counted; the overlap is double-counted until resolved.
Two elements with different IDs have identical type, section and geometry. Both are counted until resolved.
The snapshot contains no elements.
A dimension exceeds a configurable plausibility band. Quantities are still computed as given.
An opening does not intersect its host. It deducts nothing.
An opening lies partly outside its host. Only the part inside the host is deducted.
The element type is outside the quantity scope (e.g. Tendon, Link). It is skipped.
A column axis lies inside a wall. Both are counted in full (no deduction).
Steel comes from an estimated ratio, not from bars or design output.
Element steel rate exceeds the configurable high-rate band.
The input 'exact' flag contradicts the reinforcement source. The engine reports exactness derived from the source.
An element appears more than once with identical content. The first copy is kept, later copies are excluded.
A warning reported by the extractor/source was passed through. Subject = the source's own code.
An analytical segment or mesh element whose physical parent exists was excluded to avoid double counting.
Openings in one host overlap each other. Their union is deducted, not their sum.
The element's material is structural steel; it is not part of concrete quantities.
Steel was derived from required design areas, not from provided bars.
No steel material was named; the configured default density was used.
